mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC60 T5 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement Volvo XC60 T5 engine typically costs £2,800-£5,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £3,500-£6,500 depending on labour rates. The B4204T11 is the most common T5 engine in UK XC60s. Used engines: £800-£1,800. Reconditioned: £1,800-£3,500. Rebuilt with warranty: £2,800-£5,500. Fitting labour: 8-12 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: How much does a Volvo XC60 T6 engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Volvo XC60 T6 engine replacement (B4204T29) costs £5,000-£8,000 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, reflecting the twin-charged complexity. The supercharger alone is a significant cost component. Used engines: £1,500-£3,000. Reconditioned: £3,500-£5,500. Rebuilt with warranty: £5,000-£8,000. Fitting labour: 10-14 hours at £65-£100/hr.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Volvo XC60 T5?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value. For a 2013-2017 XC60 T5 worth £5,000-£14,000, a £2,800-£5,500 rebuilt engine is usually worthwhile if the car is otherwise sound. For a 2010-2013 example worth under £4,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective. Cars worth £8,000+: rebuilt engine with warranty is recommended. Cars worth £4,000-£8,000: evaluate both options. Cars worth under £4,000: consider used engine or scrap.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of supercharger failure in a Volvo XC60 T6?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include loss of power at low revs (where the supercharger provides boost), a rattling or grinding noise from the engine, and reduced throttle response. The supercharger clutch failing to engage is a known issue. Loss of low-end power. Unusual noises from the supercharger area. Check engine light with boost-related codes. Supercharger seal failure can also cause oil leaks.

mainEntity.name: Is the Volvo XC60 T5 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - overall, the XC60 petrol/hybrid models scored 96.5% in the What Car? Reliability Survey, outperforming the diesel variants (92.6%). However, the B4204T7 and B4204T11 engines have a known oil consumption issue due to piston ring design, and timing chain tensioner wear can occur at higher mileages. Petrol XC60: 96.5% reliability score. Regular oil changes (every 8,000-10,000 miles) are critical. B4204T11 oil consumption typically appears from 70,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the XC60 T5 and T6 petrol engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T5 is a 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder producing 240-245 hp. The T6 is either a 2.0-litre twin-charged (turbocharger + supercharger) producing 306-310 hp, or in early models (2014-2016) a turbo-only 2.0-litre. The later B4204T29 T6 combines a roots-type supercharger for low-end response with a turbocharger for high-end power. T5 (B4204T11): 245 hp, turbo only, FWD or AWD. T6 (B4204T29): 310 hp, turbo + supercharger, AWD only. T6 Polestar Engineered: 326 hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Volvo XC60 T5 / T6 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The T5 and T6 petrol badges have been part of the Volvo XC60 range since the first-generation (P3) model launched in 2009, evolving from a 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo to the sophisticated Drive-E family with supercharger and turbocharger combinations. The T6 badge initially denoted a 3.0-litre six-cylinder before moving to a twin-charged 2.0-litre four-cylinder in the second-generation (SPA) XC60 from 2017.

milestones.description: B4204T7, 2.0-litre turbo petrol, 240 hp - first-generation XC60 T5 launch
B4204T11, 2.0-litre turbo petrol, 245 hp - facelift update with increased power and improved emissions
B4204T9, 2.0-litre turbo petrol, 306 hp - first 2.0-litre T6 (twin-charged) introduced in the XC60
B4204T29, 2.0-litre turbocharged and supercharged petrol, 310 hp - second-generation SPA platform XC60 T6 AWD with 8-speed Geartronic
B4204T15, 2.0-litre turbo petrol, 220 hp - lower-power T5 variant for select markets
B420T (mild-hybrid) - electrified B-series petrol engines begin replacing pure T5/T6 badging

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every petrol engine fitted to the Volvo XC60 T5 and T6 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Volvo XC60 T5 / T6 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Volvo XC60 T5 and T6 petrol engines - particularly the B4204T7, B4204T11 and B4204T29 - are broadly well-regarded, but they have specific, well-documented failure points. Petrol XC60s scored an impressive 96.5% in the What Car? Reliability Survey, but when failures occur, they tend to be serious. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - Why the Volvo XC60 T5 B4204T7 and B4204T11 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Piston ring carbon buildup leads to bore glazing, allowing oil past the rings into the combustion chamber. A 2016 XC60 T5 owner reported oil consumption from 70,000 miles, with Volvo acknowledging a "design defect" but no recall. The B4204T11 has been specifically cited for "design defects, parts quality issues".

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical decarbonisation to free stuck piston rings
repairOptions.longevity: May buy 10-20k miles; not a permanent fix

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full strip-down, new piston rings, cylinder honing
repairOptions.longevity: Effective but labour-intensive; 50-80% of replacement cost

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded rings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value if keeping car 2+ years

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2017 XC60 T5 is worth approximately £5,000-£14,000 depending on mileage and condition. For a sub-£6,000 example, a used engine or piston ring repair may be more cost-effective. For cars valued above £8,000, a rebuilt engine with warranty typically justifies the premium.
problems.recommendation: If your XC60 T5 is burning more than 1 litre of oil per 1,000 miles and you plan to keep the car, a rebuilt engine with upgraded piston rings is the definitive fix. The £2,800-£5,500 cost is significant but represents good value against a £5,000-£8,000 dealer repair for the same work. For lower-value examples (under £4,000), consider a quality used engine or evaluate scrap value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B4204T11 Volvo XC60 T5 engine prices

problems.h4: Supercharger Failure - Why the Volvo XC60 T6 B4204T29 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The roots-type supercharger has internally lubricated bearings that eventually fail. The supercharger clutch can fail to engage, requiring the whole unit to be replaced. T8 PHEV supercharger seals can also fail, hampering performance.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace clutch mechanism only (if available separately)
Supply & fit rebuilt unit with upgraded supercharger, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If engine has other issues or high mileage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2017-2021 XC60 T6 is worth £14,000-£38,000. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value; a rebuilt engine is financially viable for most owners.
problems.recommendation: For T6 owners, a supercharger replacement (not a full engine) is usually the right call if caught early - the engine itself is generally robust. Supercharger clutch failure is a known weakness; replacing the supercharger unit at £1,800-£3,000 specialist cost is far cheaper than a full engine. If the engine has suffered consequential damage from supercharger failure, a rebuilt unit with warranty becomes the better option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B4204T29 Volvo XC60 T6 engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Camshaft Issues - Volvo XC60 T5 / T6 Petrol
problems.affectedModels: Volvo XC60 T5 and T6 (all B4204T variants)
problems.rootCause: The VEA petrol engines use a timing chain rather than a belt. While generally durable, chain tensioner wear and camshaft seal failure have been reported. Camshaft issues accounted for a significant portion of engine complaints in later XC60 models.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: If chain has snapped causing valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a 2013-2017 XC60 T5 worth £5,000-£14,000, a £1,200-£2,000 timing chain replacement is a sensible preventative investment. For a 2010-2013 example worth under £4,000, evaluate whether the repair is justified.
problems.recommendation: If your XC60 T5 or T6 has reached 80,000 miles and you have no record of timing chain work, preventative replacement is strongly advised. A snapped timing chain on a VEA petrol engine typically destroys the cylinder head and valves, turning a £1,200 repair into a £3,000-£5,000 engine replacement.
